st: Pour [[3 cups]] of the water into a heavy pot and bring it to a boil over medium-high heat.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] of the cornmeal with the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until it is a smooth, thin paste.
Stir the paste into the boiling water with a wooden spoon. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it forms a thin porridge.
Add the salt if using. Cover the pot and let it bubble on low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the rest of the cornmeal a handful at a time, stirring hard after each addition to keep out lumps.
Keep stirring and pressing the mixture against the side of the pot for 5 minutes until very stiff and smooth.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 5 minutes to steam through.
Scoop the nshima into a wet bowl, turn it to shape a smooth mound and serve hot with relish. Pinch off a piece, roll it in your fingers and use it to scoop the relish.
Grind the peanuts in a food processor until fine and powdery. Stir [[0.5 cup]] of the water into the ground peanuts to make a smooth paste.
Put the washed spinach in a pot with [[0.5 cup]] of the water and the salt. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until wilted and tender.
In a second pot, heat the oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until they have broken down into a soft sauce.
Stir in the cooked spinach and any liquid in the pot.
Pour in the peanut paste and the remaining [[0.5 cup]] water. Stir well.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Taste for salt and serve hot with nshima.
Rinse the dried fish well in cold water to remove grit. Soak in [[1 cup]] warm water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish in a single layer for about 3 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Lift out and set aside on paper towels.
Wipe out the pan and heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, salt and pepper. Cook for 8 minutes until soft and saucy.
Return the fish to the pan and stir gently. Cook for 3 minutes so the fish soaks up the sauce.
Serve hot with nshima.

ing: dried and ground into flour; sold as chikanda or orchid tuber flour
st: Grind the roasted peanuts to a fine powder in a food processor.
Mix the orchid tuber flour, ground peanuts, chili powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Heat the water in a heavy pot until warm, not boiling. Whisk in the flour mix a little at a time to stop lumps forming.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until very thick.
The mixture should look like a stiff paste that pulls away from the side of the pot.
Grease a loaf pan, press the hot paste into it and smooth the top.
Cool, then chill for 1 hour until firm.
Turn out the loaf and cut it into slices.
Serve cold as a snack, or fry the slices in a little oil until crisp. Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Rinse the dried caterpillars several times in cold water, then soak them in [[2 cups]] warm water for 30 minutes to soften.
Drain, then boil in [[1 cup]] fresh water with a pinch of the salt for 10 minutes. Drain well and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, the remaining salt and chili powder if using. Cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Stir in the caterpillars and coat them well in the tomato mixture.
Fry over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring often, until browned at the edges and slightly crisp.
Serve hot with nshima.

ing: skin on, cut into serving pieces
st: Season the chicken pieces all over with half of the salt and the black pepper.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for about 4 minutes per side, then set it aside.
In the same pot, cook the onions for 7 minutes over medium heat until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and bell pepper and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until they collapse into a sauce.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the water and the remaining salt.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F (74°C).
Uncover and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the gravy. Taste and add salt.
Serve hot with nshima.
